name: MARLIN: Mixed-Precision Auto-Regressive Parallel Inference on Large Language Models
affiliations: Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA)
problem: 4-bit weight quantization speeds up single-stream decoding because it cuts memory traffic, but the speedup evaporates once you batch many concurrent clients, which is the regime real serving runs in - the batch becomes compute-bound and the low-precision tensor-core path is not used.
mechanism: A mixed-precision (FP16 x INT4) weight-only quantized GEMM kernel that keeps FP16 activations and FP16 accumulate in the tensor cores and dequantizes INT4 weights on the fly in shared memory, using a fused lookup-table dequant scheme so the extra ALU work overlaps with tensor-core work instead of serializing. The K dimension is processed in tiles so the kernel holds its speedup at batch 16-32 rather than degrading.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim: ~4x speedup over FP16 PyTorch on an inference-optimized NVIDIA A10 GPU for large matrices at batch sizes up to 16-32, decaying to ~1.5x at batch size 128 as the problem becomes compute-bound. Sparse-MARLIN (a separate variant) improves further at high sparsity.
